description: Interpret the forcing process as a monotone cellular automaton on the product grid behind a constructible graph. Each cell stores a quotient module of reachable label vectors after modding out support already absorbed into T, and infection occurs when the anti-diagonal line intersects that local module.
mathematical_formalization: Let L_t <= (Z^2)^V be the submodule generated by the initial seeds R and all edge-difference generators exposed by G up to time t. Define T_{t+1} = T_t union {e in V : exists f in L_t with supp(f) subseteq T_t union {e} and f(e) = a(1,-1), a != 0}; the CA surrogate tracks M_t(e) = pi_e(L_t / (Z^2)^{T_t}).
analogical_connections: Bootstrap percolation where infection is algebraic rather than purely Boolean.
Gaussian elimination executed by local update rules on a lattice.
Reaction-diffusion with the anti-diagonal line acting as the trigger threshold.
implementation_hypothesis: Represent each local module by a small Smith-normal-form state or a reduced basis over bounded coefficients. Simulate updates on candidate d_1 x ... x d_k grids, and use the exact verifier only after the CA surrogate predicts complete forcing.
experiment_seed: Fix a small slope alphabet X with 4-6 nonzero vectors, enumerate tiny product grids, and compare surrogate infection closure against an exact global linear-algebra implementation.
novelty_claim: The new step is to encode arithmetic Kakeya forcing as a quotient-module infection process with a genuinely local state representation, making CA-style search plausible without discarding exactness.
differentiation: This is not another asymptotic Kakeya argument or another generic bootstrap-percolation paper. The target object is a concrete constructible certificate with score minimization, and the state variable is an integer module tied to the verifier semantics.
